problem: The sentence 'At a branching junction in steady flow, the volume flows into the junction add up to the volume flows out' is written as if it holds for any steady flow. Volume balance needs constant density as well; a gas junction must be balanced on mass. The exam-trap list corrects this later, but a student reading only this paragraph can be misled.
fix: At a branching junction in steady flow of an incompressible fluid, the volume flows in add up to the volume flows out, ΣQ_in = ΣQ_out. For a gas, balance mass instead: Σṁ_in = Σṁ_out.

problem: 'Gases keep the density' is ambiguous. It can be read as 'the density of a gas stays constant', which is the opposite of the point being made, and it clashes with the very next sentence about air at 5 bar being denser than at 1 bar.
fix: For a gas you cannot cancel ρ; keep it in the equation: ρ₁A₁V₁ = ρ₂A₂V₂. Air at 5 bar is roughly five times as dense as air at 1 bar, so a gas main that loses pressure along its length speeds up even when the area does not change, while the mass flow stays the same.
